title: Made my first AI game demo. now what
author: EntertainmentNew1789
selftext:
I started this around a month ago. 

I picked a 2D pixel farming game because Stardew has owned my brain for years. This is a practice project and I’m not planning to sell it.

A few weeks went into research. The actual build took around a week. Farming and fishing work. Mining is half alive and the NPCs can say a few things.

I thought getting this far would feel better tbh.

My asset sizes are all over the place. The house looks huge next to the road. I resize it, look at the river again, somehow the whole area got worse. Nothing connects cleanly and I’m getting tired of looking at it.

Lately I open the project and stare at it for ten minutes. Maybe resize the same house again. Then I close it because I still don’t know what the next useful task is.

well, garbage achieved lol

If anyone has an idea what I should work on first, I’d really appreciate it. I’m terrible at figuring out priorities.

https://reddit.com/link/1vxp4gr/video/2ms607yd1glh1/player

comments.author: Zzpasta
comments.body:
Honestly, this is really impressive for a first attempt, especially after only a few weeks of research and about a week of actual development! You already have farming, fishing, mining, NPC dialogue, inventory/UI, etc. working — that's a lot.

If I were prioritizing, I'd focus on **visual consistency before adding more features**:

1. **Fix the pixel-art scale** — make sure the player, house, trees, road, crops, etc. use a consistent pixel size.
2. **Fix the character sprites** — especially the white/background pixels appearing around the walking animation.
3. **Redo the mine map** — It looks grid-like. Make the floor/walls feel like one cohesive environment rather than individual tiles.
4. **Improve the UI** — the current UI works, but it doesn't quite match the pixel-art world yet. A consistent pixel font, borders, colors and panel style would help a lot.
5. Then worry about more content.

I'd recommend watching **AdamCYounis – Pixel Art Tutorials** on YouTube, especially his videos about tilesets, environments and pixel-art fundamentals. [AdamCYounis on YouTube]()

Don't scrap it though — you've already got a solid prototype. **I'd spend some time polishing what you have rather than starting over.**

replies.author: EntertainmentNew1789
replies.body: Thank you, I really appreciate this. I’m still new to there, but you put into words something I’d already been feeling. I’ll check out the video you mentioned. I was honestly very close to starting over.
